title: Graded access scoring for plan lanes with preemption windows
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Implement a new admission scoring function for plan lanes (free / paid / enterprise) that dynamically ranks incoming requests for allocation to limited inference capacity. The scorer is quota-aware, region-aware, and supports short preemption windows to protect enterprise commitments while maximizing overall acceptance and fairness across tenants.
background: We currently use a simple priority-first lane allocation that strictly favors enterprise lanes and then best-effort paid/free lanes. This results in poor utilization during variance, bursty tenant behaviour, and hard drops for paid plans that temporarily exceed expected traffic patterns. Previous tickets focused on soft-reserve and spillover policies; this work consolidates those ideas into a compact scoring approach that is easier to reason about, test, and roll out incrementally.
proposal: Introduce a graded admission score computed per-request and evaluated by the admission controller. Score components: 1) normalized quota_balance (remaining tokens / expected tokens), 2) burst_budget (short-term allowance derived from moving-average consumption), 3) sla_weight (customer tier weight), 4) regional_affinity_penalty (if cross-region), 5) fairness_adjustment (to boost long-starved tenants), 6) randomize tie-breaker. Use a sliding preemption window that reserves a configurable fraction of capacity for enterprise weight for the next N seconds; outside that window admission is purely score-driven. The controller will admit until capacity is exhausted, then probabilistically accept lower-score requests when admission headroom is available via decay-driven credits.
algorithm_pseudocode:
function compute_score(request):
  q = clamp(request.quota_balance / expected_balance, 0.0, 2.0)
  b = min(1.0, request.burst_budget)
  s = request.sla_weight  // enterprise: 3.0, paid: 1.3, free: 0.8
  r = region_penalty(request.region, pool.region)  // 0.0 for same region, up to -0.3 for remote
  f = starvation_boost(request.tenant_id)  // small adaptive boost if tenant has been served less than target
  jitter = rand_uniform(0, 0.01)
  score = q * 0.45 + b * 0.25 + s * 0.2 + f + r + jitter
  return score

Admission loop:
  sort pending requests by compute_score desc
  reserve = capacity * enterprise_reserve_fraction if within_preemption_window()
  allocate to enterprise until reserve filled or no enterprise requests
  allocate remaining capacity by descending score; if scores tie within eps, use jitter
  when under heavy load, probabilistically accept score<threshold with p = score/score_max to smooth sharp cutoffs
acceptance_criteria:
1) New scorer computes scores and logs decision metadata for each admission event.
2) Unit tests covering edge cases: negative balances, zero burst budget, cross-region penalties.
3) Integration test simulating mixed free/paid/enterprise traffic shows reduced enterprise tail latencies and improved paid acceptance by >= 6% compared to baseline under same capacity.
4) No SLA violations for enterprise (less than 1% priority drop) during canary period.
5) Telemetry fields available in Console: admission_score, components:{quota_balance,burst,burn_rate,region_penalty,sla_weight,starvation_boost}.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 - bench & unit tests (2w): implement scorer behind feature flag, collect synthetic metrics.
Phase 1 - shadow canary (1w): run scorer in shadow for 1 region, compare decisions to prod router.
Phase 2 - live canary (2w): enable for 5% of traffic in us-west1 with monitoring and automated rollback.
Phase 3 - staged rollout (3w): ramp 5%->25%->60%->100% per region with kill-switch.
Phase 4 - tuning & cleanup (2w): retire shadow mode, cleanup flags, docs and runbook updates.
metrics: Primary: enterprise_drop_rate_p90, paid_acceptance_rate, free_accept_rate, cluster_utilization, admission_decision_latency_p99. Secondary: model_token_error_rate, fairness_index (Gini over accepted-per-tenant), rollback_count.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for score math and starvation_boost decay.
2) Simulator: reproduce diurnal and heavy-burst patterns; compare admission curves vs current allocator.
3) End-to-end load test with model shim and capacity-limited pool, assert no regression in p99 response time.
4) Chaos test: kill a subset of workers during canary to validate graceful fallback.
5) Security & privacy check: no tenant secrets logged; review telemetry fields for PII.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: mis-calibrated weights could starve free/paid customers or breach enterprise SLAs. Mitigation: conservative default weights, short canary with enterprise reserve, automatic rollback triggers based on enterprise_drop_rate and paid_acceptance_rate. Risk: increased decision latency under high qps. Mitigation: precompute some components (quota_balance, burst_budget) in per-tenant cache and limit per-request computation to a few ops; add p99 admission_decision_latency alert. Risk: behavioral complexity for SREs. Mitigation: concise runbook and dashboards showing component contributions for top tenants.
notes: This design is intentionally compact to make A/B comparisons straightforward. We avoid large stateful queues in favor of score-based admission so the policy can be deployed incrementally and observed via existing telemetry. The starvation_boost uses an exponential backoff decay window so short tenants with bursty traffic don't gain long-term advantage.
